## Writing guidance and author choices

**Reuse established story memory — John, 11 September 2026.** Routine writing sessions start from the already-built ledger, dossiers and structural maps. Read new or changed material, consulting original passages only for a specific evidence need or ambiguity. History stays excluded unless deliberately restored; do not reread the full core or historical corpus per session. Verify that default commit with no source change makes zero extraction calls and that a new or edited registered passage extracts only changed scenes, without unchanged or historical recapture. Guidance alone does not prove this runtime behavior.

Use [project onboarding](references/onboarding.md) and [first writing session](references/first-writing-session.md). Read coherent story units with common book/trilogy/series context; a book ledger and master ledger are views of one source-qualified store. For collections, keep unrelated fictional worlds distinct. Current manuscript and content/version evidence establish source priority; a Bible is useful but fallible, and newer author direction outranks old interpretations. Keep written material, planned revision, possibilities, historical versions and unexamined material distinct. Do not return to the obsolete 469-heading capture, tiny-heading model calls or a whole-series reread.

Every meaningful book/story/collection unit, intermediate group such as a trilogy, and whole work needs an explicit theme and governing structure.
